sections.h2: Two counties, two sets of offices
sections.html:
Morristown is the seat of Hamblen County. City Hall handles city tax and code enforcement, while the courthouse holds the assessor, the trustee and the Register of Deeds. A slice of Morristown lies in Jefferson County, so find out which county holds your parcel before dialing anyone.

The city had 33,517 residents in mid-2025, up 10.2 percent from 2020. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $181,100, and owners live in 54.9 percent of them. Median rent is $882 a month. With values that modest, even a small repair bill eats a visible share of the sale price. Investors will compare what you ask with the rent figure.

Morristown houses draw a city bill and a Hamblen County bill. Both rest on the same assessment roll, at 25 percent of the assessor's appraised figure.

Where and when Morristown owners pay
BillWhere to payDates
City of MorristownCity Tax Office in City Center, weekdays 8 to 5, or the drop box in the City Center parking garageNotices late September, 2 percent off in October, no penalty through February 28
Hamblen CountyTrustee at the courthouse, the office at 2415 North Davy Crockett Parkway, or TNPayments.comBilled October 1, delinquent March 1

Phone payments are not accepted at the city office. Questions about the county bill go to the Trustee at (423) 586-6290. The Assessor of Property works from the courthouse at 511 West Second North Street.

Round up these papers before the first offer arrives:

  • Your last city receipt from the City Tax Office and your county receipt from the Trustee.
  • Your deed, which the Register of Deeds can copy from records that start in 1860.
  • Permit papers for a roof, furnace, water heater or addition.
  • Notes on any open Codes Enforcement complaint.
  • Names and lease dates for tenants, if there are any.

Ownership is recorded as of January 1 each year, which is why an autumn bill can still carry your name after you sell. Put the division with the buyer in writing.

Your first stop is the Assessor's office, the contact point for the county Board of Equalization. The board listens to owners who believe land or building values are off. County boards convene each June 1. The State Board deadline is August 1 or 45 days after the county notice, whichever is later. Phone the Assessor at (423) 586-1852 for this year's filing date.

The buyer receives the next bill, so mention any pending appeal during negotiations.

Two codes officers look into each complaint, normally within a day. A confirmed violation brings a certified letter and 14 to 21 days to fix it. After that the city can take the owner to City Court, or send a contractor to mow or clean up and attach a lien to the parcel. Your title agent should search for liens like that.

Permits are needed for a new roof or windows, gas, electrical, plumbing or HVAC work, additions, sheds, carports and pools over 24 inches deep. Building Inspections answers at (423) 585-4626. The usual violations are tall grass, junked vehicles, roof holes and unsafe decks. City rules also forbid sleeping in a camper, shed or any structure not built for living.

An open complaint on your house should be fixed or disclosed. Call Codes Enforcement at 423-585-1830 to check the status.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Hamblen County
sections.html:
Hamblen County's Register of Deeds is on the third floor of the Administrative Building at the courthouse, phone 423-586-6551. Records go back to 1860, and the office collects the state's two recordation taxes. A sale carries a realty transfer tax of 37 cents per $100 on the higher of price or value, and the buyer taking title pays it.

If part of your parcel lies in Jefferson County, ask which register applies before you sign.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when you sell
sections.html:
A fall closing in Morristown can land between the two bills. City notices go out in late September and the county bill on October 1. Close after that and the printed bill may still show your name, though the buyer owns the property.

The title agent splits each bill by the days you held the house. Request a written statement of what was paid and divided, and keep it with your closing papers in case a bill turns up months later. If a city or county bill is delinquent when you list, the balance is paid from your proceeds, and the 2 percent October discount no longer applies once that month has gone by.

Two offices means two calls. Get a payoff figure or a paid receipt from the City Tax Office and from the Trustee, and hand both to the closing agent.

Owners live in only 54.9 percent of Morristown homes, so rentals are common. If a tenant lives in yours, pull the lease, the rent and the end date before you talk to buyers.

Some investors will keep a tenant in place, and they will measure your price against the local median rent of $882. A tenant who lives in a camper, shed or other structure not built for living can cause a code problem, since city rules forbid it. Clear that up before a buyer or inspector notices.

Listing the house can earn a better price if it shows well, yet you face open houses, a buyer's loan approval and an inspection that may reopen the price. Selling for cash gives up some of that upside in return for speed and a firm closing. With code complaints, a tired roof or an uncooperative tenant, plenty of owners here pick the firm closing.

Either way, the same four offices touch the file, so keep their phone numbers handy through closing day: the City Tax Office, the Trustee, Codes Enforcement and the Register of Deeds.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
With no lender involved, the sequence is brief.

  1. You describe the address, the condition and any lease.
  2. An offer comes back, and you accept it in writing.
  3. A title agent checks the deed, searches for city liens from cleanup work and requests tax payoffs.
  4. At the signing the deed goes to Hamblen County for recording, and the tax bills are divided.
  5. Proceeds are paid out after any liens, back taxes and mortgage balance are cleared.

Damp winters with freeze cycles wear on exterior wood, gutters, roof flashing and crawl-space vents, and a lender's inspector will flag every one. Buyers paying cash accept the house as found, so you can skip that repair chase.

faqs.q: When do I pay Morristown city taxes?
faqs.a: Statements show up in late September. Pay during October for 2 percent off, or pay by the following February 28 and owe nothing extra. Phone payments are not taken.

faqs.q: Does Hamblen County send a separate tax bill?
faqs.a: The county collects on its own through the Trustee. Billing starts October 1 and March 1 is the delinquency date. Online payment is at TNPayments.com.

faqs.q: What if my Morristown house has an open code case?
faqs.a: Resolve it before listing, or tell the buyer. The city gives 14 to 21 days to comply, then may file in City Court or clean the lot itself and lien the parcel.

faqs.q: Where is a Morristown deed recorded?
faqs.a: Call 423-586-6551 for the Hamblen register. A parcel that straddles into Jefferson County may need that county's register instead, so ask first.

faqs.q: Which Morristown repairs need a permit?
faqs.a: Roofs, windows, gas lines, wiring, plumbing, HVAC, additions, sheds and deep pools all qualify. Building Inspections, (423) 585-4626, can confirm before you start.
